W: Excuse me, but wasn't the express train to Ashford scheduled to leave at eight thirty?

M: It was, but a signal failure on the northern line has forced the transport authority to halt every departure.

W: I understand. So no trains will run at all today?

M: Technicians expect to clear the fault within two hours. Service should resume normally once that's done. Your pass stays valid until nine.

W: All right. I suppose I'll pick up a coffee across the street.

M: Bellamy's does wonderful almond pastries, if you're hungry.

M: Hello. I'm Devrim. We spoke over the phone this morning about an estimate for redoing the floor in your shop.

W: Oh, hello. Please come in. Yes, I'd like the dark floor in the hallway changed to something lighter.

M: Certainly. But I should point out that the estimate could come in higher than you're expecting, because taking off the old dark finish means a good deal of extra work.

W: That makes sense. And will you need to take the display cabinets out of the hallway before you begin?

M: That won't be necessary. We can cover them with plastic sheeting.

passage_text:
W: Hi. It's my first time stopping by. What a bright space! You seem to have a lot of new furniture and equipment here.

M: We do. We opened our doors only this month. The standing desks, meeting rooms, and printing stations you see are all brand-new.

W: Wonderful. I'm thinking about signing up. My clients are all based two streets away.

M: Well, here's a leaflet setting out our membership tiers. I'd be glad to go over any of them with you.

W: Thanks. I do run workshops a couple of times a month. Is there a room I could book?

M: There is. Why don't we begin with a walk around so you can see everything we offer?

M: Hello, Ms. Halvorsen. I appreciate you making time today to go over your operation. What's your top priority this year?

W: Well, over the past few months my garden center has been getting far more online orders through our Web site. Knowing what those customers think of the plants they've chosen really matters to me.

M: We could build you an automated follow-up survey. It goes out by text two weeks after a delivery arrives, and we've found people are unusually willing to fill those in.

W: That's very appealing. I might even let anyone who fills one in reserve next season's plants early.

M1: Excuse me, Ms. Okafor. My technician, Rahim, is still up on the roof checking the ventilation system, but I wanted to let you know we're nearly through.

W: How is it all looking?

M1: Actually, here's Rahim now. He can tell you himself.

M2: I checked the whole system. There's no damage to the main unit. Everything inside it is in good condition, but several filters were damaged by the heat, and we'll have to replace those.

W: Well, that's a load off my mind. I'd been dreading a complete replacement.

M2: Unfortunately you'll have to shut the kitchen while we change the filters over. We can wrap it up within a single day, though.

M1: Would Thursday suit you?

W: That works for us.

W: Vậy thì tôi nhẹ cả người. Tôi đã lo là phải thay toàn bộ.

M2: Tiếc là chị sẽ phải đóng cửa khu bếp trong lúc chúng tôi thay bộ lọc. Nhưng chúng tôi có thể làm xong trong đúng một ngày.

M1: Thứ Năm có tiện cho chị không?

W: Thứ Năm thì được ạ.

M: Hi, Maya. I'm sorry I couldn't make the budget briefing this morning! My drive in was dreadful.

W: Don't worry about it. The minutes will go around later. What went wrong?

M: The county's resurfacing the harbor bridge, and it's tacked another forty minutes onto my drive. Traffic in both directions is squeezed into a single lane, and driving is the only way I can get here!

W: Well, there's a passenger ferry that crosses every half hour.

M: I had no idea. I've only just relocated to the county. Where can I read up on it?

W: I'll pass along the timetable and the fare chart from their site.

M: Chào Maya. Xin lỗi vì sáng nay tôi không dự được buổi họp ngân sách! Chuyến lái xe đến chỗ làm của tôi tệ khủng khiếp.

W: Không sao đâu. Biên bản sẽ được gửi cho mọi người sau. Có chuyện gì vậy?

M: Hạt đang làm lại mặt đường cầu cảng, và việc đó khiến tôi mất thêm bốn mươi phút lái xe. Xe cộ cả hai chiều bị dồn vào một làn, mà lái xe lại là cách duy nhất tôi đến đây được!

W: À, có một chuyến phà chở khách chạy qua nửa tiếng một lần đấy.

M: Tôi không hề biết. Tôi mới chuyển đến hạt này thôi. Tôi có thể tìm hiểu về nó ở đâu?

W: Tôi sẽ gửi anh bảng giờ chạy và bảng giá vé lấy từ trang của họ.

M: Of course. What happened?

W: A strip of the vinyl at the front edge of the stage has come loose, and it kept catching people's shoes. It made the whole sequence look unsteady, and the long costumes only hid it from the front. Is there anything you can do?

M: As it happens, I've already ordered a fresh roll. It ought to arrive tomorrow.

W: Wonderful. Thank you. I can hardly believe opening night is next week. Everyone has poured so much into this show — it'll be wonderful to see it performed for a full house.

M: Morning, Beatriz. The invitation for the staff conference landed in my inbox. I'm surprised it's in April this year rather than November.

W: Right, we shifted the dates so we could try this lodge out. I went and looked it over in February and came away very impressed. The catering in particular is outstanding. There was nothing free in November, though.

M: I'm sure the switch will be worth it. Your training team always plans good events.

W: Here, I've just brought up their page. Have a look. Staff pick one of these workshops for the second afternoon.

M: I've never tried nature photography. This looks like a good chance to give it a try.

M: Chào Beatriz. Thư mời hội nghị nhân viên đã vào hộp thư của tôi. Tôi khá bất ngờ là năm nay hội nghị vào tháng Tư chứ không phải tháng Mười một.

W: Đúng vậy, chúng tôi đã dời ngày để thử khu nhà nghỉ này. Tôi đã đến xem hồi tháng Hai và rất ấn tượng. Đặc biệt là dịch vụ ăn uống thì xuất sắc. Mà tháng Mười một thì không còn chỗ trống nào cả.

M: Tôi tin là sự thay đổi này sẽ đáng giá. Nhóm đào tạo của chị lúc nào cũng tổ chức sự kiện tốt.

M: Tôi chưa từng thử nhiếp ảnh thiên nhiên bao giờ. Đây có vẻ là cơ hội tốt để thử.

Ashvale Airport to Add Quiet Rest Lounges

By Nadia Krause, Transit Monthly

Ashvale International Airport has unveiled a plan to significantly improve the experience of transit passengers. Recognizing that waits of two hours or more are common among passengers with connecting flights, who account for roughly 35 percent of daily traffic, the airport management has decided to add more food counters and to install sound-insulated rest booths in Terminal 3.

The refurbishment project consists of two main stages. Stage 1 involves the rebuilding of the Market Hall to offer better food choices and is scheduled to be finished by 14 October. Once the food area is fully functional, Stage 2 will begin, converting the waiting area beside Gate 40 into the new Quiet Zone. Management expects the whole project to be complete before the winter travel season.

NOTICE: Refurbishment Update

Posted on 14 October

We would like to update passengers and staff on the progress of the ongoing facility renovation at Ashvale International Airport. Please be advised that the Market Hall is scheduled to reopen in three weeks.

In addition, work on the Quiet Zone will start next week. Please note that the general waiting area beside Gate 40 will be closed off. The Ashvale Club Lounge, on the upper floor of Terminal 3, will however stay open and accessible to all eligible passengers while the work goes on.

A good layover despite the building work
By: Miguel Sandoval
Date: 20 October

I had a four-hour layover on my way to a trade fair, and I was relieved to find that the lounge on the upper floor of Terminal 3 was still running. I was able to access by showing my Air Travel Rewards card, and it gave me a quiet place to work and enjoy a light meal.

Also, as I arrived at Terminal 1, I used the shuttle bus to get across to Terminal 3 for my connecting flight. Since my flight got in very late, I was glad the shuttle runs at every hour of the day and night.
